query: Owner deducted 25,000 for repainting the entire apartment even though there was only normal wear and tear over my 2 year stay.

model_output.summary: Your landlord has deducted 25,000 rupees from your deposit for repainting the entire apartment. Under the law, tenants are not responsible for normal wear and tear and are only liable for damages exceeding it.
facts_extracted: Stayed in the apartment for 2 years
The condition of the apartment only had normal wear and tear

options.title: Send a Formal Written Request/Notice
options.description: Write a formal message or letter to your landlord citing the rules against charging for normal wear and tear, and request the full return of your deposit.
pros: Often resolves the issue quickly without legal action
cons: Landlord may ignore or refuse the request

options.title: Approach District Legal Services Authority (DLSA)
options.description: Contact your local DLSA for mediation support to help resolve the security deposit dispute with your landlord.
cons: Requires participation from both parties for mediation to work
options.forum: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA / NALSA Helpline 15100)

citations.relevance: States that the tenant is only bound to restore the property subject to changes caused by reasonable wear and tear.
Mandates that security deposits must be refunded upon taking vacant possession after making legitimate deductions only for damages exceeding normal wear and tear.

missing_info: Whether there is a written rent agreement specifying painting clauses
Photographic evidence of the apartment condition at move-in and move-out
